items.title: Education Department repeals the vacated 2024 Title IX rule and restores the prior text
items.summary: The Education Department’s final rule repeals the 2024 Title IX amendments and restores the pre-2024 regulatory text in the Code of Federal Regulations. The department says the 2024 rule was vacated nationwide and has gone unenforced for more than eighteen months, so the change recodifies the law currently in force rather than creating a new substantive policy. The rule took effect immediately on September 29.

items.title: SBA removes affirmative-action provisions it calls unnecessary and potentially unlawful
items.summary: SBA’s final rule removes provisions requiring affirmative action from applicants or recipients in several agency programs, describing them as unnecessary and potentially unlawful, and makes related technical corrections. The notice frames the revision as eliminating constitutional concerns rather than changing eligibility through new factual findings. Because the rule took effect on publication, it immediately changes the regulatory terms attached to affected Small Business Administration programs.

items.title: ITC bars imports of ink cartridges found to infringe five U.S. patents
items.summary: Following summary determination by an administrative law judge, the International Trade Commission found a Section 337 violation involving five ink-cartridge patents. It issued a general exclusion order against infringing imports and cease-and-desist orders against Mountain Peak and Straightouttaink, then terminated Investigation 337-TA-1451. The Commission affirmed the initial determination with supplemental findings and modified reasoning; the notice reports an adjudicative finding, not merely an allegation.

items.title: Commerce renews Ural Airlines’ temporary denial of U.S. export privileges
items.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security
items.summary: Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security renewed Ural Airlines’ temporary denial of export privileges, finding renewal necessary to prevent an imminent violation of the Export Administration Regulations. The order says the Russian carrier has engaged in repeated, ongoing, or continuous apparent violations and recounts successive renewals since the original October 2022 order. “Apparent” is the agency’s characterization; the order is preventive export-control relief, not a criminal conviction.

items.title: IRS proposes four-year installment rules for tax on qualified farmland sales
items.publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury and Internal Revenue Service
items.summary: Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service propose rules for a statutory election allowing tax on gains from sales or exchanges of qualified farmland to qualified farmers to be paid in four equal annual installments. The proposal would define and administer the election for sellers who qualify; comments and hearing requests are due November 30. The rule is consequential for farm transfers because it changes payment timing, not the amount of gain treated as taxable.

items.title: Census releases county-level 2024 data on businesses without paid employees
items.summary: Census released 2024 Nonemployer Statistics covering businesses with no paid employees, federal income-tax liability, and at least $1,000 in receipts—$1 for construction. The administrative-data series reports establishment counts and receipts across eighteen 2022 NAICS sectors and from the national level down to counties, with selected legal-form and receipts-size breakdowns. Census notes that most U.S. establishments are nonemployers, chiefly self-employed sole proprietorships.

items.title: DTC proposes AnnounceDirect for submitting corporate-action announcements
items.publisher: The Depository Trust Company and U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
items.summary: The Depository Trust Company proposed AnnounceDirect, a modernized process for agents to submit corporate-action announcements, with related changes to the operational arrangements governing how securities become and remain eligible for DTC services. The proposal concerns the infrastructure by which agents transmit event information into the central depository. The Securities and Exchange Commission published the filing to solicit comment; it has not approved the rule change.

items.title: ITC keeps oil-country tubular-goods trade orders after five-year reviews
items.geography: United States / India / South Korea / Turkey / Ukraine / Vietnam
items.summary: After full five-year reviews, the International Trade Commission determined that revoking countervailing-duty orders on oil-country tubular goods from India and Turkey, or antidumping orders covering India, South Korea, Turkey, Ukraine, and Vietnam, would likely cause continuation or recurrence of material injury to a U.S. industry within a reasonably foreseeable time. One commissioner dissented only as to Ukraine. The determinations preserve the trade-remedy orders rather than imposing new ones.

items.title: Living-donor reimbursement no longer depends on the organ recipient’s income
items.summary: HRSA finalized revised eligibility guidelines for its Living Organ Donation Reimbursement Program after Congress enacted the Honor Our Living Donors Act in February 2026. The statute bars the agency from considering the organ recipient’s household income when deciding whether a living donor qualifies for reimbursement. The September notice responds to comments on HRSA’s July proposal and makes the statutory change operative in the program’s finalized guidance.

items.title: HUD proposes revisions to the scoring of physical housing inspections
items.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
items.summary: HUD proposes revisions to the scoring notice used under the National Standards for the Physical Inspection of Real Estate, the framework for evaluating conditions in federally assisted and insured housing. The agency is seeking comment on revised scoring procedures before issuing a final notice; comments close November 30. Because inspection scores can affect enforcement and property status, the document concerns how observed deficiencies are translated into administrative consequences, not the underlying inspection standards alone.

items.title: HRSA funds a maternal-care resource kit for incarcerated women
items.summary: HRSA awarded $750,000 in supplemental fiscal 2026 funding to JSI Research & Training Institute, the Alliance for Innovation on Maternal Health technical-assistance center, to develop a resource kit for providers and correctional custody and health staff serving incarcerated pregnant, birthing, and postpartum women. Congress directed the work in the report accompanying the 2026 appropriations act. The notice funds development and implementation; it does not report evaluated health outcomes.

items.title: FDA clears a regulatory path for generic 500-milligram sulfadiazine tablets
items.summary: FDA determined that 500-milligram sulfadiazine tablets were not withdrawn from sale for safety or effectiveness reasons. That legal and scientific finding permits the agency to approve abbreviated new drug applications for the product if applicants satisfy all other requirements. The notice does not itself approve a generic or declare the drug risk-free; it removes one threshold obstacle to generic entry based on the history of the discontinued listed product.

items.title: FAA opens environmental scoping for as many as 76 annual Starship launches from Cape Canaveral
items.summary: FAA opened scoping for a supplemental environmental impact statement on SpaceX’s proposed Starship–Super Heavy operations at Cape Canaveral’s Space Launch Complex 37. The proposal would allow up to 76 launches and 152 landings annually, split between boosters and Starship vehicles and including return-to-site and ocean landings. FAA has not reached an environmental finding; comments on alternatives, impacts, and relevant studies are due October 14 before a draft supplement is issued.

items.title: FAA releases draft environmental assessment for a higher New Glenn launch cadence
items.summary: FAA released a draft environmental assessment for Blue Origin’s proposed increase in New Glenn launch cadence at Cape Canaveral’s Space Launch Complex 36A and opened public comment. The notice announces review rather than a final environmental determination, and the agency scheduled a virtual public meeting for October 22. The document provides a current planning record for evaluating the local effects of more frequent heavy-lift commercial launches from the spaceport.
